subject: gray wolf
title: A Wild Wolf Pulled a Crab Trap Out of the Sea in 3 Minutes

scenes.text: Fishermen kept finding their crab traps torn apart. The thief wasn't a seal.
On the coast of British Columbia, a hidden camera finally caught it: a wild female wolf.
She waded in, grabbed the rope by its float, and pulled a fully sunken trap onto the beach.
Then she tore it open and ate the bait. The whole job took about three minutes.
A second wolf was filmed doing the same in 2025.
Scientists say it may be the first tool use ever seen in a wild wolf. The thief had a plan.

description:
On the central coast of British Columbia, Heiltsuk Guardians kept finding damaged crab traps. In May 2024 a camera filmed a wild female wolf pulling a submerged trap ashore by its buoy line, tearing it open and eating the bait in about three minutes.
A second wolf was filmed with traps in 2025. A study in Ecology and Evolution (2025) suggests it could be the first evidence of tool use by a wild wolf, though that is not proven.
What other animal would you suspect of stealing from fishermen?
thumbnail_text: A WOLF ROBBED A CRAB TRAP
first_comment: She knew to pull the float, not the trap. Is that tool use, or just a very smart wolf?
